thought.text: All three are "not answering yet" after 12m40s — slower than the first run. Let me inspect the dev server logs to see what they're doing:

reasoning_content:
Interesting — this time, none of the dev servers responded within 12 minutes 40 seconds. That's strange, since in the previous run, app and cms were ready in about 3.5 minutes. Something is different.

Wait — `just serve` is still alive and keeps monitoring after outputting the URL table ("not responding yet" — that table is output when the readiness deadline expires, and monitoring continues after that). The message "still running and possibly just slow" suggests the dev servers are still building/running.

What's different from the first `just up` run? In the first run, app was ready in 3 min 21 sec, cms in 3 min 18 sec. In this run, all three didn't respond within 12 min 40 sec.

Hmm — could it be that the dev servers are contending for CPU with something? Or... wait, is `just serve` holding stdin from `/dev/zero`? `/dev/zero` provides infinite null bytes. Vite reads stdin, so... Vite's CLI shortcuts only bind when isTTY. But does Vite do `stdin.resume()` on the dev server? Let me think. Actually, if Vite reads stdin and receives an infinite stream of NUL bytes... hmm, actually Vite doesn't continuously read stdin.

No wait — there's a more likely cause: memory. 7.6 GiB of RAM. 3 Angular dev servers (nx/vite) each using around 1–2 GB, plus the container. The first `just up` run succeeded in building the three (app, cms, boards compiled while the backend image was being built). Now all three are building simultaneously again, with the Gradle daemon gone... memory should be fine.

Let me look at the dev server logs to see what's going on.
